- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–5), then underestimates later; apply a slight upward bias to mid-to-late forecast days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts; if model is 5%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1 and -1, model tends to misalign with true trend; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) for correction.
